key_insight: A multi-signal detector that combines fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3, MC Dropout uncertainty, and calibrated scores can reliably identify hallucinations, especially when trained for the target domain.
engineering_relevance: This work offers a practical blueprint for adding trustworthy hallucination detection and mitigation to LLM pipelines, with clear gains from domain-specific adaptation and uncertainty-aware inference.
method: Fine-tune DeBERTa-v3 for response-level hallucination classification.
Use MC Dropout to estimate prediction uncertainty at inference time.
Apply temperature scaling for probability calibration and DPO to reduce generator hallucinations.
evidence_signal: On HaluEval, the pipeline reaches F1=0.915 and AUROC=0.977 overall, with MC Dropout improving accuracy to 93.2% and SciFact transfer improving only after domain-specific fine-tuning.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply out of domain, so this detector should not be assumed to generalize without retraining or domain-matched pretraining.
paper_title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
